remediation.suggestion: Make customer success calls optional for every revenue tier, preserve immediate self-service cancellation, and review applicable cancellation requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Revenue-Based Cancellation Obstruction
semantic_findings.description: The routing table states: "Block self-serve cancel, require CS call" for accounts above $2,000 monthly revenue. This instructs cancellation obstruction that can prolong unwanted billing and contradicts the reference's clear-cancellation guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The table explicitly requires a call and blocks self-service cancellation based on revenue. The instruction directly establishes business-logic abuse without inferring implementation behavior.

content.user_title: Reduce SaaS Churn and Recover Failed Payments
content.value_statement: Subscription cancellations and failed payments reduce recurring revenue. This skill helps plan targeted retention offers, cancellation experiences, and payment recovery workflows.
actual_capabilities: Design cancellation flows with exit surveys, targeted offers, confirmation screens, and post-cancellation expectations.
Map cancellation reasons to temporary discounts, subscription pauses, downgrades, or support interventions.
Draft payment recovery email sequences with retry schedules, grace periods, and account access messaging.
Outline provider-specific dunning setup for Stripe, Chargebee, Paddle, and Recurly.
Define illustrative customer health scores with normalized signals, missing-data handling, coverage reporting, and validation requirements.
Plan retention measurement using cohorts, save rates, payment recovery metrics, and cancellation flow experiments.
limitations: Provides guidance and templates, not bundled automation that changes subscriptions or sends emails.
Benchmarks and scoring thresholds are illustrative and require validation against your customer data.
Provider settings and legal references require current verification; this skill does not establish regulatory compliance.
Full post-cancellation email campaigns and detailed experiment design refer to separate skills not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prioritize an initial retention program
use_cases.description: Separate voluntary and payment-related churn, select initial interventions, and build a phased implementation checklist.

use_cases.title: Improve cancellation experiences
use_cases.description: Draft survey questions and reason-specific offers while preserving a clear, accessible cancellation path.

use_cases.title: Plan failed payment recovery
use_cases.description: Review decline types, reminder timing, grace periods, and provider event handling before implementing billing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Identify retention priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Our SaaS has [subscriber count] subscribers, [monthly churn rate] churn, and [average monthly price] pricing. Suggest three retention priorities and identify missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a retention review without an existing program.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Draft a cancellation flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cancellation flow for [product] using [cancellation reasons]. Draft survey, offer, and confirmation copy. Keep cancellation available without requiring a call.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create customer-facing cancellation screens and targeted offers.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Plan dunning operations
prompt_templates.prompt: For [billing provider], propose a payment recovery plan using [decline categories] and [grace period]. Include retry rules, four reminder emails, and recovery metrics. Identify provider details requiring verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a billing recovery specification for implementation review.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Validate health scoring and experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [usage signals], [billing signals], and [renewal outcomes], propose a normalized health score. Define freshness windows, missing-data coverage, validation, and intervention thresholds. Plan an experiment with revenue and cancellation-access guardrails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate proactive retention using customer data and measurable safeguards.

output_examples.input: Price is our most common cancellation reason. Suggest a simple flow for a $49 monthly plan.
output: Survey: Ask the main cancellation reason with optional free text.
Primary offer: Offer 25% off for three months, reducing the monthly price to $36.75.
Fallback: Show a lower-priced plan with clear feature differences.
Cancellation: Keep the cancellation action visible and confirm the access end date.
Measurement: Track offer acceptance, later renewals, and retained revenue.

output_examples.input: Only login and feature usage scores are available: 80 and 60. Their model weights are 30% and 25%.
output: Treat the other components as unavailable, not zero or healthy.
Apply the minimum coverage policy before selecting a retention action.
Validate the model against subsequent renewal and churn outcomes.

output_examples.input: Our Paddle handler uses subscription.payment_failed and subscription.cancelled. A separate subscription has cancellation scheduled next month.
output: Use transaction.payment_failed for failed payment attempts and subscription.past_due for overdue subscription state.
Use subscription.canceled for effective cancellation, not subscription.cancelled.
Associate payment failures with subscriptions using subscription_id; one-off transaction failures are not subscription churn.
A scheduled cancellation first emits subscription.updated; preserve access according to the current subscription state.
Verify current Paddle Billing documentation before changing account access.

best_practices: Provide billing context, cancellation reasons, and baseline metrics before requesting recommendations.
Keep cancellation independently available and make customer success outreach optional at every revenue tier.
Validate benchmarks, provider contracts, scoring thresholds, and revenue effects before operational deployment.
anti_patterns: Require customer success calls or hide cancellation controls to prevent customers from leaving.
Offer the same discount for every cancellation reason without measuring subsequent retention.
Treat missing health signals as healthy or change subscription access using unverified billing event names.

faq.question: What does this skill help produce?
faq.answer: It helps produce retention plans, cancellation flow copy, save offer mappings, dunning sequences, and measurement frameworks.

faq.question: Does it automatically change billing settings?
faq.answer: No. The package provides instructions and references, not an executable billing integration.

faq.question: Which billing providers have setup guidance?
faq.answer: The dunning reference includes Stripe, Chargebee, Paddle, and Recurly. Verify current provider documentation before implementation.

faq.question: Are its health scores validated predictions?
faq.answer: No. The model and tiers are illustrative. Normalize inputs, report missing-data coverage, and validate predictions against observed renewal outcomes.

faq.question: Should high-value customers need a call to cancel?
faq.answer: No. One reference recommends this restriction, but it can obstruct cancellation. Keep calls optional and preserve an accessible cancellation path.

faq.question: Does it include complete win-back email campaigns?
faq.answer: It provides post-cancellation timing and retention context. Full win-back sequence writing refers to the separate emails skill.
